Hi Arielle — thanks for the summary and the call earlier. Short answer: we can onboard a Malta-based vendor, but procurement requires the following to clear the PO gate: 

- Completed W-8BEN-E (signed) — we use this to document foreign status for tax withholding.
- A bank confirmation letter showing your entity name and account details (dated within 90 days).
- Evidence of authorized signer (PDF of passport or corporate signer letter) if the person signing the W-8 is not on record.
- A brief entity structure note if you have multiple legal entities / subsidiaries.

Operational items 
- Please confirm the exact legal name you want on the PO (it must match your bank letter).
- If you expect the first invoice in USD, confirm whether your bank supports USD payouts to avoid FX delays.

Im attaching our vendor onboarding checklist and W-8BEN-E template with redlines we typically accept. Once we receive the signed W-8 and bank letter, Procurement (Marissa) will triage the PO; normal sequencing is: review -> conditional PO (staged) -> final PO issuance after verification. Marissa, Jordan — looping you in to queue the vendor.

Diego Fernandez
Senior Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com

- PO value and line items match the SOW discussed; payment term is Net30 from invoice receipt.
- Please submit invoice referencing PO #67890 to invoices@redwoodinference.com and copy ap-portal@redwoodinference.com.
- If you invoice in EUR, our payments team will convert per the transaction date FX. Confirm preferred currency if you want EUR settlement.

Next steps for you: upload the signed PO and the bank letter to our vendor portal (link included in the onboarding checklist we sent). Jordan will send the portal invite and a follow-up with a ticket ID (PROC-1023) if further KYC flags occur.

If you prefer to e-sign the PO, we can send a DocuSign link; otherwise treat the attached PDF as the official PO.

Thanks — looking forward to kicking off the engagement.
